name: Agnikandadi Ghrita

sections.overview: Agnikandadi Ghrita – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction:
Agnikandadi Ghrita is a classical Ayurvedic medicated ghee prepared by processing digestive, deepana (appetising), and arsha-hara (hemorrhoids relieving) dravyas (herbs) in a combination of coconut oil and buffalo ghee along with milk-based and alkaline media. The formulation is traditionally indicated in Arsha (hemorrhoids), Pravahika (chronic dysenteric condition), and Gudabhramsha (rectal prolapse). The preparation integrates Ushna (hot), Tikshna (penetrative), and srotoshodhaka (channel cleansing) substances with nourishing sneha (oil) dravyas to support correction of impaired digestion, regulation of Apana Vata (subtype of vata dosha), and stabilization of anorectal tissues. 
 The formulation describes preparation of medicated ghrita through classical Sneha Paka procedure using herbal decoction, milk, alkaline substances, and kalka dravyas. It is administered internally in measured doses with suitable anupana.

प्रवाहणं गुदभ्रंशं शीघ्रमर्शश्च नाशयेत् । 
अर्शीरोगचिकित्सायां श्रेष्ठमेतद्भिषग्जितम् ।। 

 The verse describes preparation of medicated ghrita using Chitraka (Plumbago zeylanica), Sariva (Hemidesmus indicus), and Surana (Amorphophallus paeoniifolius) with milk, alkaline substances, and sneha dravyas, indicating its utility in anorectal disorders.
sections.composition:
I. Kvatha Dravyas (Decoction Ingredients) 

 Chitraka Mula (Plumbago zeylanica – Leadwort Root) 
 Sariva Mula (Hemidesmus indicus – Indian Sarsaparilla Root) 
 Vana Surana Kanda (Amorphophallus paeoniifolius – Elephant Foot Yam Tuber) 
 Water 

 II. Anyadrava Dravyas (Liquid Media) 

 Goksira (Bos taurus – Cow’s Milk) 
 Tusodaka (Rice Husk Water – traditional fermented medium) 

 III. Sneha Dravyas (Lipid Media) 

 Narikela Taila (Cocos nucifera – Coconut Oil) 
 Mahisha Ghrita (Buffalo Ghee – clarified butter from buffalo milk) 

 IV. Kalka Dravyas (Paste Ingredients) 

 Yashtimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra – Licorice Root) 
 Devadaru (Cedrus deodara – Himalayan Cedar) 
 Sarja Kshara (Alkaline preparation from Vateria indica) 
 Yavakshara (Alkaline preparation from Hordeum vulgare) 
 Pippali (Piper longum – Long Pepper Fruit) 
 Mayura Tuttha (Purified copper sulfate preparation as per classical reference) 
 Bharangi (Clerodendrum serratum – Bharangi Root) 
 Indrayava (Holarrhena pubescens – Kurchi Seed) 
 Malkangani (Celastrus paniculatus – Intellect Tree Seed) 
 Vidanga (Embelia ribes – False Black Pepper) 
 Bakuchi (Psoralea corylifolia – Bakuchi Seed) 
 Ela (Elettaria cardamomum – Cardamom) 
 Dhanyaka (Coriandrum sativum – Coriander Seed) 
 Kalajira (Nigella sativa – Black Cumin) 
 Ajamoda (Trachyspermum ammi – Ajwain Fruit) 
 Surana Kanda (Amorphophallus paeoniifolius) 
 Citraka (Plumbago zeylanica) 
 Arabi / Alupaga (Colocasia esculenta – Taro Tuber) 
 Shambuka Mamsa (Snail meat as described in classical reference) 

 Method Of Preparation 
 A decoction is prepared from Citraka Mula (Plumbago zeylanica), Sariva Mula (Hemidesmus indicus), and Vana Surana Kanda (Amorphophallus paeoniifolius) by boiling in water and reducing to one-fourth. The decoction is transferred to a suitable vessel and combined with Goksira and Tusodaka. Kalka is prepared from the specified kalka dravyas. Narikela Taila (Cocos nucifera) and Mahisha Ghrita are added to the mixture along with the prepared kalka and decoction. 
 The formulation is processed over mild heat following classical Sneha Paka (oil preparation) procedure, traditionally initiated on Krishna Chaturdashi and completed on Amavasya with invocation of Lord Dhanvantari. After completion of ghrita siddhi lakshanas, the preparation is filtered and stored in airtight containers. 
 Method Of Use 

 Internal administration.
sections.pharmacological_actions:
Deepana and Pachana supportive action (appetising and digestive) 
 Arsha-hara supportive effect (helps in hemorrhoids) 
 Vata-anulomana supportive action (regulation of vata dosha) 
 Srotoshodhaka supportive action (channel cleansing) 
 Shothahara supportive action (anti-inflammatory) 
 Grahi supportive action for intestinal stability 

 Clinical Indications 

 Arsha (hemorrhoids) 
 Pravahika (chronic dysenteric condition) 
 Gudabhramsha (rectal prolapse) 
 Anorectal functional instability 
 Chronic digestive impairment associated with Vata dosha aggravation 

 Therapeutic Properties 
 Citraka Mula (Plumbago zeylanica) exhibits Deepana, Pachana, and Vata-Kapha shamaka supportive properties that enhance digestive fire. Sariva Mula (Hemidesmus indicus) provides Pitta-shamaka and shothahara supportive effects. Vana Surana Kanda (Amorphophallus paeoniifolius) supports Arsha-hara action and improves anorectal function. Yashtimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra) contributes soothing and vrana-ropana supportive properties. Devadaru (Cedrus deodara) exhibits Vata-Kapha shamaka action. Pippali (Piper longum) enhances bioavailability and digestive activity. Alkaline substances such as Sarja Kshara and Yavakshara support srotoshodhana and reduction of pathological accumulations. Narikela Taila (Cocos nucifera) and Mahisha Ghrita (buffalo ghee) provide Snigdha (unctuous), Brimhana (strengthening), and stabilizing support to anorectal tissues.
sections.precautions:
Administer under supervision of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner. 
 Use cautiously in individuals with hypersensitivity to potent ingredients. 
 Follow prescribed dose and anupana. 

 Conclusion 
 Agnikandadi Ghrita represents a classical Ayurvedic formulation designed for internal administration in anorectal disorders characterized by impaired digestion, tissue weakness, and aggravated Apana Vata. The integration of Citraka Mula (Plumbago zeylanica), Sariva Mula (Hemidesmus indicus), Vana Surana Kanda (Amorphophallus paeoniifolius), and multiple supportive kalka dravyas processed in Narikela Taila (Cocos nucifera) and Mahisha Ghrita (buffalo ghee) provides a preparation intended to enhance digestive capacity, support intestinal stability, and promote normalization of anorectal function. When prepared according to classical method and administered appropriately, this formulation is regarded as a specialized therapeutic ghrita for management of Arsha, Pravahika, and Gudabhramsha.
